words.meaning: to overlap or interlock closely, like roof tiles
words.example: The new privacy rules imbricate with several existing security requirements.

words.meaning: not settled by the available facts because more than one explanation or solution fits
words.example: The cause of the sales dip remains underdetermined because the data supports several explanations.

words.meaning: based on an explicitly chosen definition or condition rather than ordinary usage
words.example: For this report, we use a stipulative definition of an active customer: anyone who logged in this month.

words.meaning: to bend something passing through a medium, or to reshape an idea through a particular perspective
words.example: The documentary refracts the housing debate through the experiences of three families.

words.meaning: to spread into branches or develop into increasingly complex consequences
words.example: A small change to the billing rules can ramify across finance, support, and compliance.

phrases.term: get out in front of it
phrases.meaning: to address a problem early before it becomes harder to control
phrases.example: We should get out in front of it and notify customers before the delay becomes public.

phrases.meaning: to add spin or a skillful twist to a ball, shot, or action
phrases.example: He put some English on the pool ball so it curved away from the corner pocket.

phrases.meaning: to criticize a decision afterward, when the outcome is already known
phrases.example: It is easy to Monday-morning quarterback the launch, but the team had limited information at the time.

phrases.meaning: an all-out, highly committed attempt with little hesitation
phrases.example: Once the pilot results came in, the team went full send on the nationwide rollout.

phrases.term: keep it in your back pocket
phrases.meaning: to save an idea or option for possible use later
phrases.example: Keep the discount offer in your back pocket in case the client hesitates.
